tagline.en: Say what you can, must and should do
tagline.bn: কী পারো, কী করতেই হবে, কী করা উচিত — বলো

subtitle.en: Every card has a short rule and 3 questions. Learn can, must, should and might, then use them to talk about the past.
subtitle.bn: প্রতিটি কার্ডে ছোট্ট নিয়ম আর ৩টি প্রশ্ন। can, must, should, might শেখো, তারপর অতীত নিয়ে কথা বলতে এগুলো ব্যবহার করো।

hint.bn: তুমি কি পারো? আমি কি পারি?

rule.en: Use can + verb for what you are able to do now, and could + verb for what you were able to do in the past. No “to”, no -s.
rule.bn: এখন যা পারো তার জন্য can + verb, অতীতে যা পারতে তার জন্য could + verb। “to” বা -s বসে না।

recap.example: I can swim. · She could read at four.

questions.prompt: When I was five, I ___ ride a bike.

options.why: “When I was five” is the past, so use could.
must means it is necessary, not that you were able to.
No “to” after a modal. Say could ride.

questions.explanation: Ability in the past: could + verb.

questions.prompt: Rina ___ three languages.

options.why: Modals never take -s, even with she or he.
No “to” after a modal.
After can, the verb stays in its base form: speak.

questions.explanation: can + base verb, the same for every subject.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means the same as “He is able to fix computers”?

options.why: must means he has to, not that he is able to.
should is advice, not ability.
After can, use the base verb: fix.

cards.badge: Can I…? · Could you…? · May I…?

rule.en: Use can, could or may to ask for permission or to ask someone to do something. can is casual; could and may are more polite.
rule.bn: অনুমতি চাইতে বা কাউকে কিছু করতে বলতে can, could বা may। can সাধারণ; could আর may বেশি ভদ্র।

recap.example: Can I sit here? · May I come in, sir?

questions.prompt: Which is the most polite way to ask for water?

options.why: This is an order, not a request.
This tells, it doesn’t ask, and it can sound rude.

options.text: Could I have some water, please?

options.why: This is fine with friends, but could … please is more polite.

questions.explanation: could + please is the politest choice.

questions.prompt: You ask your teacher: “___ I leave early today, sir?”

options.why: must is for rules, not for asking permission.
“Will I leave early?” asks about the future, not for permission.
“Do I leave early?” asks about a habit or plan, not for permission.

questions.explanation: May I…? is a polite way to ask for permission.

questions.prompt: Choose the polite request for “Open the window.”

options.text: Could you open the window, please?
Could you opened the window, please?
options.why: After could, use the base verb: open.

options.text: May you open the window, please?
options.why: We say May I…, not May you…, when we ask someone to do something.
This is still an order. Make it a question: Could you…?

questions.explanation: Could you + verb + please? is a polite request.

rule.en: must and have to both mean it is necessary. must often shows the speaker’s own feeling; have to often means a rule. For the past, use had to.
rule.bn: must আর have to দুটোরই মানে কাজটি করতেই হবে। must প্রায়ই বক্তার নিজের মনের কথা, have to প্রায়ই বাইরের নিয়ম। অতীতে had to।

recap.example: I must study. · We have to wear uniforms.

questions.prompt: Yesterday I ___ go to the doctor.

options.why: must has no past form. Use had to for the past.
have to is present, but “yesterday” is past.
There is no word “musted”.

questions.prompt: She ___ wake up at 6 every day for work.

options.why: With she, use has to.
“has wake” is wrong. We need has to + verb.
No “to” after a modal.

questions.prompt: Which is the past of “I must finish the report”?

options.why: must has no past form, and the verb after it stays in the base form.
There is no “musted”.

options.text: I had to finish the report.
I have to finish the report.
options.why: This is still the present.

questions.explanation: must → had to in the past.

cards.badge: mustn’t = no · don’t have to = no need

rule.en: mustn’t means it is not allowed. don’t have to means it is not necessary, so you can choose.
rule.bn: mustn’t মানে করা নিষেধ। don’t have to মানে করার দরকার নেই, চাইলে করতে পারো।

recap.example: You mustn’t smoke here. · You don’t have to come.

questions.prompt: Tomorrow is a holiday. You ___ wake up early.

options.why: mustn’t means not allowed. Waking up early isn’t against a rule.
On a holiday, waking up early is not necessary.
With you, use don’t, not doesn’t.

questions.prompt: You ___ use your phone during the exam. It’s against the rules.

options.why: This means no need, but here it is not allowed.
must means you are required to use it: the opposite.
can means it is allowed, but it is against the rules.

questions.prompt: “It is not necessary to bring food.” Which means the same?

options.why: This says food is not allowed.

options.text: You don’t have to bring food.

options.why: This says food is necessary.
This is not English. Say don’t have to.

rule.en: Use should or ought to + verb to give advice or say what is a good idea. shouldn’t means it is a bad idea.
rule.bn: পরামর্শ দিতে বা কোনটা ভালো তা বলতে should বা ought to + verb। shouldn’t মানে কাজটি ভালো না।

recap.example: You should rest. · You ought to see a doctor.

questions.prompt: You look tired. You ___ go to bed early.

options.why: mustn’t means not allowed, but going to bed early is a good idea.
can’t means not able, which doesn’t fit.
ought always needs to: ought to go.

questions.prompt: You ___ eat so much sugar. It’s bad for your teeth.

options.why: Too much sugar is bad, so the advice must be negative.
This is wrong. The negative is shouldn’t.
No “to” after should.

questions.prompt: Which means the same as “You should call your mother”?

options.why: ought always needs to: ought to call.

options.text: You ought to call your mother.
You ought to calling your mother.
options.why: After ought to, use the base verb: call.

options.text: You must to call your mother.
options.why: No “to” after must, and must is stronger than advice.

rule.en: Use may, might or could + verb when something is possible but you are not sure. might is a little less sure.
rule.bn: কোনো কিছু সম্ভব কিন্তু নিশ্চিত নও, তখন may, might বা could + verb। might-এ নিশ্চয়তা একটু কম।

recap.example: It might rain. · She may be late.

questions.prompt: Take an umbrella. It ___ rain later.

options.why: must means you are sure, but nobody is sure about rain.
has to means it is necessary, which doesn’t fit the weather.
Modals never take -s.

questions.prompt: I’m not sure, but Tanvir ___ at home now.

options.why: After may, use the base verb: be.
must be means you are sure, but you said you’re not sure.
maybe is one word that starts a sentence (Maybe he is at home). Here we need may be.

questions.prompt: Which means the same as “Maybe he is busy”?

options.why: must is for when you are sure.
After might, use be, not is.
can’t be means you are sure he is not busy.

cards.badge: must be = sure · can’t be = sure not

rule.en: Use must when you are sure something is true, and can’t when you are sure it is not true.
rule.bn: কোনো কিছু নিশ্চয়ই সত্য মনে হলে must, নিশ্চয়ই সত্য না মনে হলে can’t।

recap.example: He must be tired. · That can’t be true.

questions.prompt: She has worked for 12 hours. She ___ be exhausted.

options.why: After 12 hours of work, she is surely tired, not surely fresh.
mustn’t means not allowed. It isn’t a guess.
This is about need, not about being sure.

questions.prompt: You just ate a big lunch. You ___ be hungry already!

options.why: You just ate, so you are surely not hungry.
mustn’t means not allowed. For “sure it’s not true”, use can’t.
should is advice, not a guess.

questions.explanation: Sure it is not true = can’t.

questions.prompt: “I’m sure this is Rafi’s bag.” Which means the same?

options.why: might means you are not sure.
This means you are sure it is not his.
After must, use be.

title.en: Should Have / Must Have: The Past
title.bn: Should have / Must have: অতীত নিয়ে

rule.en: Use should have + V3 for a regret, must have + V3 when you are sure it happened, might have + V3 for maybe, and can’t have + V3 when you are sure it didn’t.
rule.bn: আফসোস বোঝাতে should have + V3, নিশ্চিত ঘটেছে বোঝাতে must have + V3, হয়তো ঘটেছে বোঝাতে might have + V3, নিশ্চিত ঘটেনি বোঝাতে can’t have + V3।

recap.example: I should have studied. · She must have left.

questions.prompt: I failed the test. I ___ harder.

options.why: The test is over, so talk about the past: should have studied.
After have, use V3: studied.
“should of” is a spelling mistake. Say should have (should’ve).

questions.explanation: Regret about the past: should have + V3.

questions.prompt: The road is wet. It ___ last night.

options.why: Last night is the past, so use must have + V3.
After have, use V3: rained.
The wet road shows that it did rain.

questions.explanation: Sure it happened = must have + V3.

questions.prompt: “I’m sure he didn’t see us.” Which means the same?

options.why: This means you are sure he did see us.
After have, use V3: seen, not saw.
This means it was wrong for him to see us.

questions.explanation: Sure it didn’t happen = can’t have + V3.
